:::{#sol-real-valued-practice}

Yes.
For every $\vx \in \reals^3$,
$2 x_1 + 5 x_2 - x_3$ is one [real number](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mcs/number-systems.html#def-real-numbers),
so $f : \reals^3 \to \reals$ is [real-valued](#def-real-vector-valued).
For example,
$f\paren{\sbmat{1 \\ 1 \\ 1}} = 2 + 5 - 1 = 6$.

:::
